title: Split allow list from allow read in firestore.rules to cap request.query.limit

evidence.quote: allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);
allow read: if isOwner(uid) || hasActiveTutorAccess(uid, profileId);

why: `allow read` grants both `get` and `list` under the identical condition on every match block in the file (learner_profiles, completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger, and every other subcollection); none constrains `request.query.limit`, so nothing stops an unbounded query. This matters most for the tutor cross-user read path: a compromised or custom client authenticated as an active tutor can issue one unlimited `.get()` query across a child's entire completions/learning_ledger history.
recommendation: Split `allow read` into `allow get` (unchanged) and `allow list` (same condition && request.query.limit <= 500) on at least the per-profile event collections (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger).
acceptance_criteria: functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs asserts a list query with an unbounded/501+ limit against completions is denied while limit(500) succeeds.

corrections: sites:23 overcounts; SR-4's actual scope ('per-profile event collections') is ~4–6 sites (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger, arguably reward_redemptions/diagnostic_logs), not all 23 allow-read clauses — most of the remaining ~17 are bounded config/snapshot/administrative collections where an unbounded list poses materially lower risk. This matches the finding's own recommendation, which already narrows to 4.
